Cautiously positive. The statement highlights strengthening activity and employment alongside continued virus-related risks, while committing to outcome-based forward guidance under the Fed’s average inflation targeting framework (Powell’s 2020 shift to a makeup strategy). This mix aligns with the New Keynesian insights of Clarida, Galí, and Gertler that expectations and credible commitments amplify policy support, and with Svensson–Woodford’s case for forecast-based targeting and “lower-for-longer” guidance at the zero lower bound. Continued QE purchases ($80B Treasuries, $40B MBS) and floor-system tools (IOER, ON RRP) support accommodative financial conditions, consistent with literature on the portfolio and signaling channels of QE, while the acknowledgment that inflation pressures are “largely transitory” and that risks remain tempers the tone. Overall, the communication is net supportive but measured rather than exuberant.
